chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Herman Stark and the gangster owners of the Cotton Club
summary: Crawford describes Herman Stark, Owney Madden and Mike Best as the strict owners and says he did not realise they were gangsters.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well now, when he came -- you said he came to the rehearsal.
Yeah. Stand back, couple of stocks. Herman Starks talking to Starks Did you -- you didn't know Elmer Stocks.
Well, he was the boss of the Cotton Club.
What kind of guy was he?
Nice fellow, but he meant business. So I bought all them drums (inaudible) Quirky Onie Madden, Mike Bess, they were all (inaudible), but they were respectful and they demanded respect from others.
Did many gangsters come to the Cotton Club?
I didn't know gangsters then, because you know they did. They owned the place. Oh, yeah. But I didn't know.
You didn't know that they were gangsters.
